markers.impact: Reduced intracellular T4-to-T3 thyroid hormone conversion
markers.interpretation: DIO2 converts inactive T4 into active T3 inside cells. The G (Ala) allele is linked to reduced conversion efficiency, which may contribute to localized tissue hypothyroid symptoms (fatigue, brain fog) despite normal serum TSH levels.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Serum thyroid measurements do not measure intracellular levels directly. Cellular T3 depends on nutrient cofactors (selenium, zinc, iron) as well.

sources.name: DIO2 Thr92Ala and Thyroid Hormone Replacement Response
sources.notes: Identifies that carriers of the Ala92 allele show preference for combination T4/T3 therapy.

markers.interpretation: GPX1 is a key antioxidant enzyme that protects the thyroid gland from hydrogen peroxide during hormone synthesis. The T (Leu) allele reduces enzyme activity, increasing thyroid oxidative stress vulnerability, particularly if selenium status is low.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Actual GPX1 activity is highly dependent on selenium status; supplementation can rescue enzyme expression levels in some genotypes.

sources.name: ClinVar GPX1 variant entry
sources.notes: Maps the GPX1 Pro198Leu variant to rs1050450.

markers.impact: Altered T-cell activation regulation / autoimmune susceptibility
markers.interpretation: CTLA-4 is an immune checkpoint receptor. The G (Ala) allele reduces CTLA-4 cell surface expression, leading to elevated T-cell activation and increased baseline predisposition to autoimmune conditions including thyroiditis.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: CTLA4 is one of many polygenic risk modifiers; environmental triggers and intestinal permeability are primary determinants.

sources.name: CTLA4 polymorphisms and autoimmune thyroid disease
sources.notes: Large association study establishing CTLA4 as a primary autoimmune thyroid locus.

markers.impact: Impaired lymphoid phosphatase regulation / autoimmune risk modifier
markers.interpretation: PTPN22 Arg620Trp (T allele) alters a tyrosine phosphatase, which compromises T-cell receptor signaling inhibition. Associated with elevated risks of systemic lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune thyroiditis.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Low prevalence but highly significant common modifier; requires clinical confirmation if autoimmune symptoms present.

sources.name: PTPN22 and autoimmune diseases
sources.notes: Seminal study mapping PTPN22 to multiple autoimmune syndromes.

markers.impact: Altered CD40 translation / thyroid antibody production
markers.interpretation: The C allele of the CD40 -1C>T translation start site variant increases translation efficiency, promoting B-cell activation and elevating baseline levels of thyroid antibodies in susceptible individuals.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Highly polygenic modifier; thyroid antibodies must be directly checked in serum.

sources.name: CD40 gene variants in thyroid autoimmunity
sources.notes: Associates CD40 promoter mutations with increased antibody production.

markers.impact: Altered thyroid stimulating hormone receptor expression
markers.interpretation: The TSHR rs179247 A allele is a replicated risk modifier associated with autoimmune thyroid diseases (such as Graves' disease and Hashimoto's), affecting receptor signaling sensitivity.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Circulating thyroid antibodies provide direct evidence of pathology, not raw array SNPs.

sources.name: TSHR variants and thyroid dysfunction
sources.notes: Details the TSHR locus contribution to genetic thyroid risks.

markers.interpretation: DIO1 is responsible for baseline peripheral deiodination. The C allele is linked to shifts in Free T4/Free T3 ratios in serum, reflecting minor variations in systemic conversion velocity.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Substrate partitioning depends on liver health and cortisol levels.

sources.name: DIO1 polymorphisms and thyroid hormone levels
sources.notes: Confirms DIO1 variants modulate circulating thyroid hormone concentrations.
